ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the horizontal axis represents succession time, from about 1 year, 25 years, 50 years, 75 years to 100 years. The vegetation sequence from left to right is, in order, bare mineral surface, then herbaceous community, next shrub community, then white pine-spruce forest, and finally beech-maple forest appears after about 75 years. Reasoning: Beech-maple forest belongs to a relatively late-stage successional community and cannot form immediately in the initial grassland stage; it needs the previous stages to gradually change environmental conditions, especially after the white pine-spruce forest forms, when the soil, shading, and microenvironment are more suitable for the growth of tree species such as maples. Therefore, beech-maple forest appears only after about 75 years.
